title: Jones's sharp ear and Joe Martinez 'Hawkeye' in the WPA band
summary: Jones heard every wrong note during lessons; Joe Martinez, called Hawkeye, did the same in the WPA band.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Did Dave Jones do anything else in the day? Have any other kind of a job, or just make a living from his music? How did he do?

Well, at that particular time, from the way that he told me that he got his foundation, well, he kind of worked it for the Gideys Foundation. He said he worked it hard, he said he worked on the regular. But at that time, he was teaching. Yeah, he was teaching. Had quite a few students? He had quite a few students. Yeah. He had quite a few students. They all knew him. He was a good musician. Yeah. Because he would be in the kitchen and you couldn't put that note on him. And he would be sitting there eating and he would take it all over your lesson. But he would get up from the table if you made one note and come tell you this is where you

You couldn't fool him, you know. No, you couldn't fool him. So we had a fellow like that down in the WPA band. And the one who played in the band at that time was Mr. Martinez. You might have heard of him, huh?
Joe Martinez. Well, now you can be playing in that band, okay, how many men was there? And if you make a wrong note, he would come and pull you out and tell you this is where you made it.

He just was that sensitive. So we called him Hawkeye. Hawkeye? Yeah, we called him. Martin. Yeah, Hawkeye. But you can see in you. So yeah, he wouldn't miss. So whenever that band was playing, don't think you're going to make something wrong, then he ain't going to know. He'd come right there and pull you out and tell you this is what you made wrong.
